title: Sweater with metallic yarn (multi-agent)
description: a women's sweater made from a blend of cotton, nylon, and metallic yarn
blurb: A blend of cotton, nylon and metallic yarn. The fiber that predominates by weight decides.
reference_excerpt: The product in question is a women's sweater identified as Style 1243047, made primarily from a blend of materials including 60% cotton, 26.2% nylon, and 13.8% metallic jersey knit fabric. The classification process involved determining the composition and construction of the garment. The outer surface of the sweater has nine or fewer stitches per two centimeters, which is a key factor in its classification under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule. The U.S. Customs and Border Protection laboratory confirmed that the fabric is composed of metalized yarn, specifically a combination of 56.2% cotton staple, 28.5% polyester filament, and 15.3% metalized mylar type knit fabric.

memo.argument: Heading 6110 covers sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts and similar articles, knitted or crocheted. The product is a complete, finished women's sweater made from a blend of cotton, nylon (man-made fiber), and metallic yarn. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made up knitted or crocheted articles, which this sweater is. Section XI Note 2(A) provides that goods of mixed textile materials are classified as if consisting wholly of the textile material that predominates by weight. The product contains cotton, nylon, and metallic yarn in a blend; without specific weight percentages stated, the classification depends on which material predominates. Under GRI 6, the subheading is determined by comparing subheadings at the same level. Subheading 6110.20 covers sweaters of cotton; 6110.30 covers sweaters of man-made fibers; and 6110.90 covers sweaters of other textile materials. Since the product is a blend without a single predominating material clearly identified, and given that nylon (a man-made fiber) is explicitly named as a component, 6110.30 (Of man-made fibers) is the appropriate subheading. Within 6110.30, the product does not contain 25% or more leather (6110.30.10), 23% or more wool (6110.30.15), or 30% or more silk (6110.30.20), so it falls under 6110.30.30 (Other). This classification is supported by ruling M85371 (in force), which classified a women's sweater with 95.6% acrylic, 2.4% nylon and 2% metallic yarn under 6110.90.9030, and ruling K85028 (in force), which classified a woman's knitted sweater with 47.5% acrylic, 17.4% cotton, 15.3% wool, 11.8% nylon, 5.3% polyester and 2.7% mylar under 6110.30.3020. Both rulings confirm that multi-fiber blends containing nylon and metallic components are classified under heading 6110. The product meets all requirements: it is a made-up, knitted or crocheted article designed to cover the upper body, and contains man-made fibers (nylon) as a significant component.
exclusions_against: Section XI Note 1 excludes certain materials (animal hair, asbestos, etc.) but none apply to this cotton-nylon-metallic blend. Chapter 61 Note 2 excludes worn clothing and orthopedic appliances, neither of which applies. No exclusions prevent classification in heading 6110.

classification.rationale: Heading 6110 clearly covers this knitted women's sweater under GRI 1, but the correct 6-digit subheading turns on which fiber predominates by weight under Section XI Note 2(A), and the description does not state percentages. Cited rulings show that similar cotton/nylon/metallic blends have been classified variously under 6110.30 or 6110.90 depending on actual composition, so a specific 10-digit code cannot be confirmed without the weight breakdown. The best-guess code 6110.30.30.20 assumes man-made fiber (nylon) predominates and that wool/silk/leather thresholds are not met, consistent with the closer-fact ruling K85028.
